uc.t: Cell Anomaly & Thermal Runaway Early Warning
d: Analyses cell/module voltages, temperatures, internal-resistance trends and (where fitted) off-gas sensors across all racks.
Detects outlier cells, abnormal self-discharge, temperature divergence and precursor signatures of thermal runaway hours-to-days ahead.
Provides rack-level isolation advisories and escalation protocol to prevent propagation.
p: BMS alarms fire at thresholds — too late for runaway precursors
One cell failure can propagate to rack/container fire
Container fire = ₹15-40 cr asset loss + site shutdown + reputational damage
Cell-level data volume overwhelms manual review
Insurance costs rising after global BESS fire incidents
uc.calc: Expected loss reduction: fire probability ~0.5-1%/yr × ₹25 cr loss × 60-70% risk reduction ≈ ₹1-1.5 cr + insurance premium reduction 10-20% + avoided shutdown days. ₹3 cr per 100 MWh per year.

d: Analyses charge/discharge curves, capacity tests, DoD/C-rate/temperature history per rack to estimate true SoH beyond BMS values.
Models degradation drivers and forecasts capacity fade under alternative dispatch profiles.
Tracks fade vs OEM warranty curve and builds evidence for warranty claims and augmentation planning.
p: BMS SoH values optimistic and inconsistent across racks
Fade above warranty curve unnoticed until capacity tests fail
Dispatch decisions ignore degradation cost per cycle
Warranty claims fail without independent SoH evidence
Augmentation capex planned on assumptions, not data
kpi: Capacity fade rate %/yr vs warranty curve
uc.calc: Warranty recovery on abnormal fade (₹1-3 cr episodic) + deferred augmentation 6-12 months × capex carrying cost + degradation-aware dispatch uplift. ₹2 cr per 100 MWh per year.

d: Analyses SoC estimate drift vs coulomb-count/OCV reconciliation, PCS efficiency curves, rack imbalance and communication faults across BMS/PCS/EMS stack.
Detects SoC estimation errors, rack imbalance limiting usable capacity, PCS derating and control-stack misconfiguration.
Provides calibration schedules and configuration fixes to recover usable capacity and round-trip efficiency.
p: SoC errors 3-8% strand usable capacity and breach obligations
Rack imbalance means weakest rack caps the container
PCS derating and efficiency loss unmonitored
BMS/PCS/EMS from different vendors — faults fall between them
RTE degrades silently below contracted values
uc.calc: Usable capacity recovery 2-4% × revenue per MWh installed + RTE improvement 0.5-1% × throughput margin. ₹1 cr per 100 MWh per year.

d: Analyses market prices (DAM/RTM), DSM signals, contracted obligations, RE co-located generation forecasts and battery degradation cost per cycle.
Optimizes charge/discharge schedules to stack revenue streams (energy arbitrage, deviation reduction, ancillary/peak obligations) net of degradation cost.
Provides automated bid/schedule recommendations and post-trade P&L attribution.
p: Dispatch run on static rules; price spreads under-captured
Degradation cost ignored — cheap cycles destroy asset value
Revenue streams optimized in isolation, not stacked
RTM volatility opportunities missed
No P&L attribution per cycle/decision
kpi: Cycles per day vs degradation budget
uc.calc: Revenue uplift 10-15% on ₹25-35 cr/yr gross revenue per 100 MWh (1 cycle/day × ₹4-6/kWh spread) net of degradation cost = ₹3-4 cr per 100 MWh per year.

d: Analyses container/room temperatures, HVAC power, chiller setpoints, ambient conditions and dispatch schedule.
Models thermal inertia and optimizes cooling setpoints/pre-cooling around planned cycles to hold cell temperature bands with minimum auxiliary consumption.
Detects HVAC faults (refrigerant loss, fan failures) degrading thermal control.
p: Auxiliary (HVAC) consumption 2-5% of throughput — direct margin loss
HVAC setpoints static; no pre-cooling before heavy cycles
Temperature excursions accelerate degradation silently
HVAC failures found on temperature alarms, after cell stress
Summer aux loads spike unmanaged
uc.calc: Aux reduction 20-30% × 3% of throughput × ₹4/kWh + degradation avoidance from tighter temperature bands. ₹0.8 cr per 100 MWh per year.

d: Integrates off-gas detectors, smoke/heat sensors, thermal cameras and CCTV CV models across containers into one safety layer.
Detects gas evolution, external thermal anomalies, unauthorized entry and suppression-system readiness gaps.
Provides automated emergency protocol triggers (isolation, ventilation, fire brigade alert) and compliance audit trails.
p: Safety sensors installed but not integrated into one decision layer
Suppression readiness unverified between audits
Emergency response depends on operator interpretation at 3 am
CEA/insurer compliance documentation manual
Access control gaps during O&M visits
uc.calc: Risk-adjusted loss reduction + insurance terms + avoided compliance penalties. ₹1 cr per 100 MWh per year.

uc.t: EMS Data Foundation & Fleet Analytics Layer
uc.vt: Enabler for all other use cases (no standalone ₹ impact)
d: Foundational layer unifying BMS (cell-level), PCS, EMS, meters, HVAC and market data across containers/sites into one historian.
Handles high-frequency cell data volumes and vendor heterogeneity; enables all analytics use cases.
Provides fleet dashboards, obligation tracking and APIs for optimization engines.
p: Cell-level data discarded or locked in vendor BMS
BMS/PCS/EMS vendors have separate portals
Dispatch decisions run on incomplete data
Fleet-level view absent across sites
Analytics blocked on data plumbing
uc.calc: Enabler — value realized through downstream use cases.
